identity.title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation

problem.claim: MLLMs struggle with knowledge-intensive tasks because their parametric knowledge is limited and outdated.

gap.claim: Although retrieval supplies external context, MLLMs often fail to fully use it during response generation, reportedly due to attention bias and conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge.

contributions.claim: Introduces ALFAR, a training-free, plug-and-play approach for improving the use of retrieved knowledge in MLLMs.
Combines relevance-based attention reallocation from visual to context tokens with output-logit decoupling and weighting of parametric versus contextual knowledge.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize ALFAR as a training-free, plug-and-play method that addresses both attention bias and knowledge conflict through complementary interventions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance across diverse datasets without additional training or external tools.
The authors report that experiments across multiple MLLMs and benchmarks consistently outperform the state of the art by large margins.
The authors report releasing code and data publicly.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLMs have limited and outdated parametric knowledge, motivating retrieval of external contextual knowledge.
Retrieved knowledge is underused; the authors identify attention bias and conflicts between knowledge sources as major causes.
ALFAR reallocates attention toward relevant context and separately weights parametric and contextual knowledge at the logits.
The authors report strong cross-dataset and cross-benchmark performance without extra training or tools.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links two diagnosed failure modes to two corresponding interventions: attention reallocation for token-level bias and logit weighting for knowledge conflict.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem-to-mechanism mapping can make a method's rationale and scope easy to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a new system, explicitly pair each diagnosed failure mode with the component intended to address it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the abstract lacks evidence that the proposed components correspond to distinct diagnosed causes.

unknowns: No numerical results, dataset names, baseline identities, or evaluation conditions are provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported superiority or the claimed causes.
